title: Exact unbounded scalar model for an ind-finite-free coefficient algebra
statement:
Let $\mathcal C$ be a site small in the coefficient universe [def-weil-size-convention], and $R$ a sheaf of commutative rings. Use module sheaves, their cochain complexes, ordinary unbounded derived categories with localization $Q_R,Q_S$, and sheafified tensor [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-pc-cochain-complex-modules, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-pur-sheaf-tensor-product]. Let $I$ be a small filtered category and assume its colimits of $R$-module sheaves are exact. Let $(S_i)$ be a diagram of commutative $R$-algebra sheaves with each underlying module isomorphic to $R^{d_i}$, $d_i\in\mathbf N$. Suppose its algebra colimit $S$, with coprojections $q_i:S_i\to S$, is also the colimit of the underlying $R$-modules [def-weil-pbc-category-colimit]. Write $E=S\otimes_R-$ for ordinary scalar extension, $U$ for restriction of scalars [def-pc-sheaf-restrict-scalars], and $E^{\mathbf L}$ for the K-flat-derived extension [lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings, def-pc-kflat-complex]. Then $E$ is exact, its termwise extension preserves every quasi-isomorphism of unbounded complexes, and its canonical derived counit is a natural isomorphism $\epsilon_A:E^{\mathbf L}(Q_RA)\xrightarrow{\sim}Q_S(EA)$ for every unbounded $R$-complex $A$. Under the K-flat model given by any resolution $p:P\to A$, this counit is $Q_S(Ep)$. There is a natural chain isomorphism
$$\kappa_A:\varinjlim_i(S_i\otimes_RA)\xrightarrow{\sim}U(EA),$$
where the colimit is termwise. On the sheafification-unit images of local pure tensors its $i$-th leg is $s_i\otimes a\mapsto q_i(s_i)\otimes a$. These identifications commute with chain maps, with inversion of quasi-isomorphisms, and with compatible maps of the coefficient diagrams. No boundedness of $A$ is required.

source.place: Tag 03EU (lemma-colimits-flat), part (2), and its tensor-colimit proof; agent refinement extracting the evaluation-normalized termwise scalar model and derived counit from the original coefficient-colimit argument. The derived extension itself is the existing lem-pur-derived-change-of-rings, not a new construction.

proof.text: Choose each finite-free isomorphism. Express its finite product of units as a finite coproduct using the finite biproduct colimit/limit isomorphism, including rank zero. Tensor preserves coefficient-sized colimits; hence left tensor by this coproduct is a finite colimit of tensorLeft of the unit. The latter is isomorphic to the identity. Finite colimits in an abelian category are exact for a finite discrete index (the colimit is also a limit), so each stage tensor functor preserves finite limits.

source.place: Tag 03EO (lemma-internal-hom-adjoint-tensor), tensor unit and additivity of Section 03EK; elementary finite-biproduct calculation

proof.text: Use the normalized extension/tensor comparison, proved privately at independent site and coefficient universes by the existing sheafification construction: identify the two presheaf tensors, sheafify, and compare restriction with sheafification after forgetting to abelian sheaves. The resulting comparison is invertible and sends each local pure tensor to itself. Naturality in the input module follows from pure-tensor extensionality. For the supplied underlying-module colimit, tensorRight of each module preserves that colimit, giving its termwise tensor cocone.

The tensor functors of the stages preserve finite limits by Step 1. Their pointwise colimit does so by the assumed exact I-colimits. Tensor preservation of coefficient-small colimits identifies this colimit functor with tensorLeft of the colimit coefficient. The ordinary comparison of Step 2 identifies it with restriction composed with E. Restriction preserves finite limits and colimits by the ordinary adjunction theorem and reflects isomorphisms through the conservative forgetful functor to abelian sheaves. Thus it reflects finite limits and E preserves them. The ordinary adjunction makes E a left adjoint, so it preserves finite colimits.

source.place: Tag 03EU (lemma-colimits-flat), part (2), using assumed exact colimits; Tag 03DA (lemma-abelian), kernels and cokernels

proof.text: Define $\kappa_A^n=\lambda_{A^n}$. Naturality of $q_i\otimes1$ for $d_A^n$ makes this a chain isomorphism from the termwise colimit to $U(EA)$. With $\eta$ the relevant sheafification unit, the $i$-th leg sends $\eta(s_i\otimes a)$ to $\eta(q_i(s_i)\otimes a)$: this is the sectionwise tensor map before sheafification, and the extension/tensor comparison preserves these images. Both orders of the differential square send it to $\eta(q_i(s_i)\otimes d_Aa)$. Equality on these images determines the sheaf maps: pure tensors generate the presheaf tensor, and the universal property of sheafification determines maps from it uniquely.

For a chain map $f:A\to B$, both naturality composites for $\kappa$ send the $i$-th pure tensor to $\eta(q_i(s_i)\otimes f(a))$. For compatible coefficient maps $h_i:S_i\to S'_i$ inducing $h:S\to S'$ with $hq_i=q'_ih_i$, the two composites send it to $\eta(h(q_i(s_i))\otimes a)$ and $\eta(q'_i(h_i(s_i))\otimes a)$, which agree. For a map along an indexing functor use the corresponding target coprojections. Presheaf generation, uniqueness through sheafification and uniqueness out of the colimit prove the squares commute. These formulas also show independence of all choices of finite free bases.

source.place: Tag 03EP (lemma-tensor-commute-colimits), canonical cocone; Section 03EK and Tag 03CY, functorial sheafified tensor maps

proof.text: By exact-functor cohomology $H^n(EA)\cong E(H^nA)$ naturally for every integer $n$. Thus for a quasi-isomorphism $f$, every $H^n(Ef)$ is invertible; $Ef$ is a quasi-isomorphism. The exact-functor factorization gives $D(E)$ and $\phi_A:D(E)(Q_RA)\cong Q_S(EA)$ naturally in $A$. Both cited statements concern unbounded complexes; no bound on $A$ is introduced.

source.place: Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor), unbounded clause and quasi-isomorphism argument

proof.text: Apply the exact-functor derived-functor theorem to E and its canonical mapDerivedCategory factorization. The supplied universal left-derived counit is then invertible on every complex. For every quasi-isomorphism p:P to A, form e as T applied to the inverse of Q(p), followed by the invertible counit at P. Counit naturality and functoriality cancel Q(p) with its inverse to prove e followed by Q(Ep) equals the counit at A. This argument applies to every P, and in particular to all K-flat P, without choosing a resolution.

source.place: Tags 06YY (lemma-derived-base-change), 06YT (lemma-derived-tor-quasi-isomorphism-other-side), K-flat resolution theorem; derived.tex Tag 015F and its left-derived dual

proof.text: Exact restriction and E preserve quasi-isomorphisms. Conjugating by the chain comparison gives quasi-isomorphism preservation for tensorColimit. Set KD to T followed by derived restriction and construct theta by composing the counit, the canonical restriction factorization, and the inverse chain comparison. For a coefficient map construct betaS by transposing the unit for the target extension through the source ordinary adjunction and the sectionwise-identity restriction-composition isomorphism. Its pure-tensor formula follows from the normalized units and scalar linearity. Restrict betaS to obtain beta, and define L by conjugation with the two supplied normalized comparisons. Pure-tensor extensionality and the cocone equation prove its required leg formula. Compose the source derived counit, Q(betaS), and the inverse target counit/restriction comparison to obtain a natural transformation after precomposition with Q. Fully faithful precomposition with localization gives betaD. Its defining equation is the displayed derived counit square, so compatibility includes all derived arrows, also inverted quasi-isomorphisms.

source.place: Section 05RR (section-derived-categories), Tag 015F (lemma-right-derived-exact-functor); categories.tex Tags 04VG and 04VK, localization uniqueness

proof_origin.place: U9 Lean proof of Stacks 03EU(2) and 03EP(2) with 03CY, exact-functor derived factorization (015F), and fully faithful localization precomposition.
